card.name: Parikaoba
card.tagline: Khevsur sword-fight dance with real blades
card.profile: Parikaoba is a warrior dance from Khevsureti in northeast Georgia (Wikipedia). A girl enters seeking her beloved; when he appears he encounters rivals, precipitating an energetic battle with sword and shield. When the girl throws down her headdress the men stop, only to renew the fight soon after. An ancient warlike dance, it has been enriched with romantic themes (the 'Khevsuruli parikaoba') and is performed on stage with real swords, men's cries and millimetre-precise acrobatic steps (georgia.travel).
card.insight: Parikaoba doubled historically as combat training in sword fighting, and dramatizes the pivotal social role of the woman whose gesture can halt the duel; its dangerous real-blade choreography featured in 'The King's Man' (2022), for which Georgian choreographer Lasha Mdzinarashvili won the Taurus World Stunt Awards Best Fight (Agenda.ge).
card.image_significance: Real-sword Khevsur duel dance. A representative image shows upright carriage, sweeping arm lines and embroidered dress — Khevsureti, Georgia.
